title: Derivative of the product Gaussian score
statement: Let $I$ be a finite index set, let $v\ge0$, and let $c,z\in\mathbb R^I$. The function $m\mapsto S_v(m,z)$, where $S_v(m,z)[h]=\sum_{i\in I}((z_i-m_i)/v)h_i$, is differentiable at $c$. Its derivative sends a direction $h$ to the linear functional $k\mapsto-\sum_{i\in I}h_i k_i/v$, with division by zero interpreted as zero.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. For $c,z,h\in\mathbb R^I$, put $S_v(c,z)[h]=\sum_i((z_i-c_i)/v)h_i$. For every $c,z$, the derivative in $c$ of $S_v(c,z)$ is the bilinear map $(h,k)\mapsto-\sum_i h_i k_i/v$.
